# The `.vcw` project schema

A VCW project is one SQLite file (§12): self-contained, movable, and
self-identifying. The schema is a deliberate superset of Audacity's AUP4 -
`sampleblocks` is reproduced column for column so that imported blocks need
no rewriting, and everything else is what Audacity has nowhere to put. See
[ADR-0001](adr/0001-project-format.md).

## Identity

| | |
|---|---|
| extension | `.vcw` |
| `application_id` | `0x56435700` (ASCII `VCW\0`) - Audacity's is `0x41554459`, `AUDY`, for *both* AUP3 and AUP4 |
| `user_version` | 1 - the schema version, a plain ascending integer |
| format version | 1 - the *meaning* of the schema, in `meta` |
| page size | 65536 bytes, set at creation |
| journal mode | WAL, `synchronous=FULL` (D3) |

Dispatch on `application_id` and `user_version`, never on the extension. AUP3 and AUP4 share an `application_id` and differ only in `user_version`, so a reader that trusts the file name is already guessing.

## Capture parameters

Blocks are **250 ms per channel** (D3, provisional from S2). The figure is a recovery-granularity decision, not a throughput one: crash loss is commit granularity plus the driver buffer, and this is the commit granularity.

Summaries match Audacity exactly - `(min, max, rms)` f32 triplets over 256 and 65536 samples. Measured overhead on a 774 MB project: 1.1%.

## Sample format codes

Audacity's encoding, `(bytes_per_sample << 16) | type_code`, extended with the two formats it has no code for. Audacity never reads a `.vcw` file, so the extension costs nothing; §8 requires 32-bit integer capture and D4 stores 24-bit verbatim rather than padded.

| code | format | bytes | origin |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x00020001` | Int16 | 2 | Audacity, identical meaning |
| `0x00030002` | Int24Packed | 3 | VCW |
| `0x00040001` | Int24Padded | 4 | Audacity, identical meaning |
| `0x00040002` | Int32 | 4 | VCW |
| `0x0004000F` | Float32 | 4 | Audacity, identical meaning |

## Tables

### `sampleblocks`

Audacity's table, reproduced exactly. Column names, types, order, the AUTOINCREMENT primary key and the absence of NOT NULL are all deliberate: tests/aup4_shape.rs diffs this against DDL extracted from a real project. Integrity is enforced next door in capture_blocks and by validate(), not by constraints that would break the match.

| column | declaration | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `blockid` | `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` | Never reused and never updated (D4). A block is written once; edits produce new blocks and leave the old ones for the undo history. |
| `sampleformat` | `INTEGER` | (bytes_per_sample << 16) \| type_code. See the format table above. |
| `summin` | `REAL` | Minimum sample value in the block, as f32. Audacity's whole-block summary. |
| `summax` | `REAL` | Maximum sample value in the block, as f32. |
| `sumrms` | `REAL` | RMS across the block, as f32. |
| `summary256` | `BLOB` | (min, max, rms) f32 triplets, one per 256 samples. The waveform pyramid. |
| `summary64k` | `BLOB` | The same, one triplet per 65536 samples. |
| `samples` | `BLOB` | The audio itself, native-endian, exactly as captured (D4: no conversion on the write path). |

### `captures`

One row per capture session (§13, §15). A session is unfinished exactly when finished_at IS NULL, which is what recovery looks for on the next launch.

| column | declaration | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `capture_id` | `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` | Stable for the life of the project; referenced by every block. |
| `sample_rate` | `INTEGER NOT NULL` | Hz, as negotiated with the device. Authoritative, unlike Audacity's project/@rate, which is only an editor preference. |
| `channels` | `INTEGER NOT NULL` | Channel count. Blocks are stored per channel, never interleaved. |
| `storage_format` | `INTEGER NOT NULL` | StorageFormat code, matching sampleblocks.sampleformat for this capture. |
| `capture_mode` | `TEXT NOT NULL` | How the stream was opened: 'exclusive', 'native' or 'shared' (§9). These are CaptureMode's three spellings; a request, not a confirmed outcome. |
| `host_api` | `TEXT` | CPAL host, e.g. 'ALSA', 'WASAPI', 'CoreAudio'. Recorded for provenance. |
| `device_id` | `TEXT` | Stable device identifier where the platform offers one. |
| `device_name` | `TEXT` | Human-readable device name at the time of capture. |
| `os_verified` | `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` | §9 and S1: bit-perfection is never claimed on CPAL's word. 0 until the platform verifier has confirmed the negotiated format against the OS. |
| `os_report` | `TEXT` | What the OS reported, verbatim, so a later reader can audit the claim. |
| `started_at` | `INTEGER NOT NULL` | Unix seconds at stream start. |
| `finished_at` | `INTEGER` | Unix seconds at clean stop. NULL means interrupted: recovery's signal. |
| `frames` | `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` | Frames committed per channel. Updated as blocks land, so it survives a crash. |
| `state` | `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'recording'` | 'recording', 'finalised' or 'interrupted'. validate() rejects anything else. |

### `capture_blocks`

The superset half: where each sample block came from and how to find it again. Audacity keeps this in its document blob; we keep it in a table, because recovery has to work from committed rows alone with no document to parse.

| column | declaration | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `blockid` | `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES sampleblocks(blockid)` | One row per sample block, sharing its key. Blocks Audacity wrote and we imported have no row here, which is how the two halves stay separable. |
| `capture_id` | `INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES captures(capture_id)` | The session this block belongs to. |
| `channel` | `INTEGER NOT NULL` | Zero-based channel index. |
| `sequence` | `INTEGER NOT NULL` | Zero-based position within the channel. Contiguous, with no gaps. |
| `start_frame` | `INTEGER NOT NULL` | Frame offset from the start of the capture. Redundant against sequence and frame_count by design: validate() checks them against each other. |
| `frame_count` | `INTEGER NOT NULL` | Frames in this block. The last block of a capture is usually short. |
| `checksum` | `INTEGER NOT NULL` | CRC32 of the samples blob, computed before the write. Detects bit rot that SQLite's own integrity check cannot see. |
| `committed_at` | `INTEGER NOT NULL` | Unix seconds at commit. Bounds how much a crash can have cost. |

### `capture_diagnostics`

§10 requires overruns, underruns, dropped frames and stream errors counted and *persisted*: they belong to the recording, not to the process that made it.

| column | declaration | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `capture_id` | `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES captures(capture_id)` | One row per capture, created with it. |
| `overruns` | `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` | Times the capture ring filled before the writer drained it. |
| `underruns` | `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` | Times the device callback found no data ready. |
| `dropped_frames` | `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` | Frames known to be lost. Non-zero means the capture is not bit-perfect. |
| `stream_errors` | `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` | Stream errors reported by the host. |
| `updated_at` | `INTEGER NOT NULL` | Unix seconds of the last update to this row. |

### `meta`

§16's four versions, plus project configuration. Key/value because the set grows with every work package and a migration per setting is not a good trade.

| column | declaration | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | `TEXT PRIMARY KEY` | Dotted key, e.g. 'created.by', 'format_version'. See meta.rs for the required set, which is checked on open. |
| `value` | `TEXT NOT NULL` | Always text. Callers parse; the schema does not pretend to types it cannot enforce. |

### `schema_migrations`

What has been applied, when, and by which build. §16 requires transactional migrations; this is the record that makes a half-applied one detectable.

| column | declaration | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` | Matches user_version once the run completes. |
| `description` | `TEXT NOT NULL` | The migration's own description, copied at apply time. |
| `applied_at` | `INTEGER NOT NULL` | Unix seconds. |
| `applied_by` | `TEXT NOT NULL` | Crate name and version of the build that applied it. |

## Indices

- `capture_blocks_timeline`
  Ordered playback and recovery both walk the timeline, and both do it per channel.

## What is not here yet

Schema v1 covers capture: blocks, sessions, diagnostics and versioning - everything milestone M1, *it records*, depends on. The vinyl data model (releases, discs, sides, tracks, boundaries), metadata, identification evidence, artwork and export settings arrive as later migrations, at WP-13 and beyond. That is what the migration machinery is for, and writing those tables now would be guessing at shapes three work packages away.
